reason: STILL BLOCKED, BUT THE RECORDED CAUSE WAS WRONG AND THE CORRECT ONE IS A DIFFERENT PIECE OF WORK. The reason this row carried - there is no post entity - is true of Postgres and FALSE of the system: the contract declares createPost(bytes32 contentHash, uint256 parentId), the chain package types a SocialPost with id, author, contentHash, parentId, blockNum and txHash, and the indexer routes GET on the social feed. PROBED LIVE THIS SESSION against the public RPC. The social-feed predeploy holds exactly 55 bytes and they are the standard proxy runtime; its implementation slot points at a second address whose code is the SAME 55 bytes, so the delegatecall lands on a proxy pointing at itself and every read reverts with a stack underflow of 5 against 6. A control call on the same endpoint answers correctly - the stable token reports 6 decimals - so this is the contract, not the node. So the schedule item is A REDEPLOY, not a schema design, and those are not the same work. NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT: contentHash is a bytes32, so the post BODY is not on chain and has no off-chain store, and the feed payload carries no author handle and no like count. Even with posts flowing, every card in this masonry would draw caption-less and author-less. The tab renders an explicit unavailable state, which is the right outcome under either cause. Frame defect unchanged: harvested 375x1365 while the registry files it at viewport 1440x900.
